source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into Windows. 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on client 5. Using folling command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>injectUpiError(socket, port, num_crcs=0, stopInj=False, cleanErrors=yes) >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record upi fatal error been detected 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log will show upi fatal error once you recover the system and boot into SEL log. 5. If there is a LCD Panel, CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Socket 0~N (Intel UPI CRC infinite on Socket 0~N error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern. Agent captures the post-injection evidence with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -180 | grep -iE 'upi|crc|infinite'; echo __UPI_CRC_infinite_on_Socket_0~N; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1".

disposition_reason: With `stopInj=False`, the injected CRC condition may persist until a separate control path intervenes; the source never supplies that path or an upper bound. Halting and resuming through ITP also makes autonomous SSH collection unreliable precisely when the fault becomes severe. Since the SUT is explicitly booted into Windows, Linux dmesg is not a valid default oracle; WHEA/ETW or vendor output must be named. A CPU-over-temperature LCD indication is not an inherent consequence of UPI CRC injection and could signal a different fault. These are specification questions, while exact tools, topology and qualified control are readiness inputs. Therefore conditional package/user-confirmed execution is appropriate, but no injection may start until the bounded contract is approved. test_case.purpose: Continuously inject UPI CRC faults at approved socket/port targets, then verify the intended fatal RAS path appears in OS, BMC and recovered UEFI evidence and in specified physical indicators without leaving the platform unrecoverable.
required_package: Exact board/CPU/UPI topology and socket-port matrix
Supported Intel ITP/CScripts package, version/hash and FAE-approved command semantics
Authorized injection duration, termination trigger and verified stop/emergency recovery path
Correct OS evidence source and expected WHEA/UPI/BMC/UEFI signatures
Front-panel and LCD applicability by SKU plus clarified LCD message
test_case.test_command: On an isolated qualified platform, an FAE/operator applies the listed EDKII settings, provisions the supported Intel ITP/CScripts environment, verifies socket/port topology, starts the exact approved `injectUpiError` sequence for a pre-authorized bounded window, stops it through the vendor method, recovers the SUT, gathers complete Windows WHEA/ITP, BMC SEL, UEFI SEL and indicator evidence, and restores settings. The current Linux `dmesg` criterion and CPU-over-temperature LCD expectation require owner resolution rather than substitution.
test_case.expected_result: 1. Check OS dmesg reports the error that match 2. BMC error log should record upi fatal error been detected 3. Front Panel fault Light will Light if there is one 4. uEFI SEL Log will show upi fatal error once you recover the system and boot into SEL log. 5. If there is a LCD Panel, CPU Over Temp error information will be displayed with details of affected CPU

safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent console and qualified FAE/operator
Snapshot settings and evidence before change; do not clear existing logs
Set a hard bounded injection window and explicit aborts for lost control, thermal/power anomaly, error storm, hang or no-boot
Never auto-retry or autonomously reset/power-cycle after loss of control
Restore BIOS settings only under the approved recovery sequence and preserve all fault evidence
expected_evidence: Harness/version/hash, exact socket-port map, command transcript and bounded start/stop timeline
Pre/post BIOS setting evidence and restoration confirmation
Complete Windows WHEA/ITP or approved OS logs, BMC SEL and recovered UEFI SEL
Timestamped front-panel/LCD evidence with SKU applicability
Abort/recovery timeline, post-recovery health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: The approved operator/agent boundary permits evidence collection but never grants autonomous authority for BIOS unlocks, ITP fault injection, resets or recovery. Missing package inputs are readiness gates, not a DUT failure.

source_conflict.reason: The procedure boots Windows but the Criteria require dmesg; an infinite injection is specified without duration or stop step; and an LCD CPU Over Temp message is required for a UPI CRC fault without explaining that mapping.
